LESSON: HUMAN REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 3.1: Human Reproductive System

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Human Reproductive System
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What are the physical, social, and emotional changes that take place during adolescence?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems
2. describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system
3. describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Human Reproductive System

Teach
• Observe Human Reproductive System in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Human Reproductive System (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Human Reproductive System.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Human Reproductive System.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Human Reproductive System.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems
• describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system
• describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Human Reproductive System.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Human Reproductive System: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the physical, social, and emotional changes that take place during adolescence?
2. How are developmental changes managed during adolescence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems
• describe functions of parts of the male and female reproductive system
• describe the physical changes that take place in boys and girls during adolescence

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
